stations.name: Amateur radio volunteers
stations.tooltip: Radio hobbyists around the world who help listen to CubeSats. Almost free, but they only hear UHF.
stations.sourceNote: CubeSat 101 sections 2.10 and 2.16: the amateur radio community often helps contact CubeSats. Pass counts are rounded estimates.

stations.name: Your own campus station
stations.tooltip: A dish you build and run yourself at a mid-latitude site. Cheap to run, but the craft only flies over a few times a day.
stations.sourceNote: CubeSat 101 section 2.10: teams build their own ground station; launching with an inadequate one is a mission killer. Pass counts are rounded estimates.

stations.name: Polar station
stations.tooltip: A rented dish far in the north. Polar orbits fly over it on almost every lap, but the Space Station orbit never comes this far north.
stations.sourceNote: High-latitude stations see polar orbits on most orbits; a 51.6 degree orbit never rises above the horizon there. Rounded rental price.

stations.name: Commercial ground network
stations.tooltip: Rent time on dishes all around the world. Lots of passes and fast data, but the most expensive choice.
stations.sourceNote: Rounded estimate for renting a worldwide ground network. For GEO the link is always on.
